stages.a: A browned block, bag stripped and flipped, a rim of bag left at the bottom.
stages.v: Fruit at 75-80% brown or more. Rinse, strip the bag leaving a rim to catch exudate, and flip the block so the wetter bottom is on top.

stages.a: White bumps rise through the brown skin.
stages.v: Pins come in stages: white bumps, then brown dots, then separating stems. Expect pins within about 2 days.

stages.a: Each bump caps over in brown: a tiny cap on a short stem.
stages.v: Brown dots follow the white bumps.

stages.a: Stems lift the caps clear of the block. A thin veil joins each cap rim to its stem.
stages.v: Bursting at 5-7 days. Shiitake is fast in the fruit room: keep it low on the racks, never above lion's mane.

stages.a: The cap rim is still curled under, and the veil is just cracking.
stages.v: Pick while the cap rim is still curled, about 6-8 days after stripping.

stages.a: The caps open flat into broad saucers.
stages.v: Picking too late is the most common mistake: flat, broad caps add weight but collapse quality and shelf life.

labels.a: The brown, leathery skin of the block.
labels.v: Buckling forms a protective skin, brown only on the outside. It lets shiitake fruit from all over the block.

labels.a: A rim of bag left at the bottom.
labels.v: When the bag is stripped, a rim of bag is left at the bottom to catch the exudate.

labels.a: White pins breaking through the skin.
A small brown cap on a short stem.
Pale flecks and scales on the cap top.
A thin veil joins the cap rim to the stem.
labels.v: Pick when the veil is just cracking.

labels.a: The cap rim still curls in toward the stem.
labels.v: Pick while the cap rim is still curled.

labels.a: The cap opens flat and thin.
labels.v: Flat, saucer-shaped caps with very thin skin soak up water and rot quickly.
